The 7-DOF arm version excludes the soccer, teaching and dance agents

The current specifications document 1.18 m, about 30 kg, 23 total DOF, one-metre-per-second walking, two-hour battery life and charging within two hours. Turning speed is separate from forward speed, and the full dimensions are not published.

The manufacturer lists approximately 1.4 m height, 31 DOF, two-hour continuous walking and a posture-dependent 10 kg dual-arm maximum. Education uses 375 TOPS compute, while Professional lists Jetson Thor T5000 at 2070 TFLOPS; optional end effectors and LiDAR remain separate.

renderedAnyboticsBoosterEvidenceCheck.scope: Thirteen ANYbotics/Booster records and216 fields; native edition ownership, battery test conditions, dual-arm posture limits, compute units, optional arm/Agent configurations and software-versus-physical ratings remain scoped. Native HTML and manufacturer README/post text only; no visual inspection.

description.after: Generation-unspecified ANYmal family reference. Manufacturer-maintained repositories separately identify ANYmal B, C and D and publish simplified ROS robot descriptions. These development assets support model visualization; extended simulation and control software require ANYmal Research membership. They do not establish one universal hardware specification for the family.

description.before: Industrial inspection quadruped with autonomous navigation, thermal, visual, acoustic and gas sensing, and integration with maintenance workflows.
description.after: Manufacturer-positioned inspection quadruped for hazardous industrial environments. The manufacturer-authored announcement describes autonomous rounds, thermal, visual, acoustic and gas sensing, and integration with maintenance workflows. The inspected post does not establish numerical mobility ratings, ingress code or a zone-specific explosion-protection certificate.

description.before: IP67 autonomous inspection quadruped with thermal, visual and acoustic sensors.
description.after: Named ANYmal D quadruped generation identified in a manufacturer-maintained robot-description repository. A simplified URDF and ROS launch files support visualization of this generation. Extended robot description, simulation and control software are restricted to ANYmal Research members; the public README does not establish current hardware specifications or availability.

description.before: Developer-focused humanoid platform for research and RoboCup soccer.
description.after: Humanoid development platform with 1.18 m standing height, about 30 kg and a documented 23-DOF configuration using four DOF per arm. The manual separates two-hour battery life from charging within two hours. Basic and Standard controllers differ, and the seven-DOF-arm variant does not support every built-in Agent.

batteryLife.after: Walking at 1.1 m/s: Geek 20 min (2 Ah); Education/Professional 70 min (5 Ah)

maxRuntime.after: 20 min Geek; 70 min Education/Professional; walking at 1.1 m/s

speed.after: Up to 2 m/s walking; runtime test uses 1.1 m/s

description.before: 95 cm / 19.5 kg education humanoid, 22 DOF, up to 200 TOPS, depth camera, ROS support
description.after: Compact humanoid development platform with a carrying handle, stereo camera and Python/C++ development tools. Geek, Education and Professional editions share the stated 95 cm height and 22 DOF but differ in compute and battery: 20 minutes walking for Geek versus 70 minutes for the 5 Ah editions at 1.1 m/s. Maximum walking speed is a separate two-metre-per-second claim.

weight.after: Approximately 42 kg; varies with version and optional configuration

handType.after: Optional standard end effectors, grippers or dexterous hands; configuration dependent

dof.after: 31: head 2, waist 3, arms 7 each, legs 6 each

payload.after: Maximum 10 kg dual-arm payload; strongly posture dependent

speed.after: 3 m/s stated walking speed; runtime test speed unspecified
